newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINA'S GUIDOTTI WARNS OF SPENDING PRESSURES.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINA'S GUIDOTTI WARNS OF SPENDING PRESSURES.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Pablo Guidotti warned Thursday that the nation's public finances are under pressure to increase spending ahead of the Octoer mid-term congressional elections.
"There are election pressures to spend more, but also pressure for faster economic growth," the official told Reuters in an interview during a banking conference.
Guidotti said the current economic growth of eight percent was encouraging certain sectors of the Peronist administration to demand extra expenditure allowances.

But he still said he was surprised by an International Monetary Fund report warning that Argentina would overshoot its $3.0 billion 1997 budget deficit goal by $500 million -- especially since it beat the first-half goal by $90 million.
"They are the Fund's forecasts and it's true the targets are tough, but we are working towards them, after reaching the goals in the first half," he said.
IMF officials alerted to what they perceive as spending pressures, and recommended corrective measures to ensure a fiscal safety margin for the rest of the year.
An IMF mission arrives in Argentina on August 20 for the annual check-up of Argentina fiscal accounts and to gauge its performance on second-quarter targets.

Guidotti also said that an extraordinary Treasury income item in July, from the sale of the 10 percent of the share capital of privatized oil company YPF that was still in employees' hands, would not be taken into account by the IMF as fiscal revenue when calculating budget targets.

But the Argentine July Treasury or central government balance did benefit from the YPF share flotation. The deficit was $198.6 million against a shortfall of $788.7 million for July last year. Fiscal income for the month rose $601 million, mainly due to $394.4 million from the YPF share flotation.
"The July result was due to us keeping control on spending and to the YPF income," Guidotti said.
